scope: Synchronous function arrays and captured array environments in recursive CPU values

implementation.admission: Synchronous structural function arrays are supported in recursive units, including array parameters and results inside callable signatures; task/fallible/device/error paths remain rejected
implementation.ownership: Checked array owners retain contiguous pair storage and each nonnull managed environment, counting duplicate edges separately; captured arrays use the same environment-record path
implementation.validation: Active descriptors and compiler-owned code/environment identities are checked before publishing an owner; inactive fields are ignored
implementation.cleanup: Bounded temporary pointer tables release on every outcome, transactional owners retain array and closure backing, and final release uses the existing iterative managed graph cleanup
implementation.limit: 300000 dependencies per array owner: one array backing and at most 299999 nonnull environment references, counting duplicates; capture-free elements consume no environment edge
implementation.separation: Existing acyclic function arrays retain their prior representation and behavior; recursive worker/error/GPU/export paths remain blocked

coverage: Named, shared and owned captured function arrays in recursive enum fields
Returned arrays, slice/concat, captured arrays and maps creating closures
Mutual record/enum immutable updates, record-array fields and higher-order function-array results
Generated LLVM boxing retains array storage and duplicate closure environments after invocation settlement
Captured String bytes survive settlement and final edge release is balanced
Inactive invalid descriptors ignored; active null, oversized, noncanonical descriptors and null/mismatched/unknown/foreign/ordinary environments rejected
Failures in temporary table, array owner and parent publication leave no live invocation allocations
Cancellation, invalid active flags, dependency exhaustion and capture-free large-array admission
Existing function-array frontend/execution and recursive source/collection/callable/runtime regressions
qualification.initial_test_correction: The first new source harness attempted reduceSum on an array; it was corrected to an ordinary checked recursive array sum. Final qualification includes all corrected cases.

documented_example.compiled_with: normal native CLI in all four new source variants

qualification.format: Changed C++ ranges formatted; new and changed recursive test files pass clang-format --dry-run --Werror; git diff --check passes

limitations: Recursive workers, parallel groups, application-error channels, fallible/task/device signatures, placement/GPU execution and public CPU bridge exports remain rejected
Retained backing after settlement does not make a settled invocation callable or implement worker transport
Private code entries are trusted compiler output, not arbitrary foreign callback addresses
Invocation-owned allocations remain retained until settlement; earlier reclamation and duplicate-edge/table compaction remain optimization work
Existing signature, work, allocation, stack, call-depth and nested array callback limits remain in force
Qualification covers selected macOS ARM64 CPU behavior, not the full suite, performance or other platforms
